newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian markets positive but thin on budget news.
newsitem.headline: Russian markets positive but thin on budget news.

text.p: Russian markets, open on Saturday and Sunday, shrugged off news that parliament had passed the 1997 draft budget in a first reading but traders said prices could firm in the coming week in thin pre-holiday trade.
Dealers on the Russian equities market said the decision by the opposition-dominated State Duma lower house to pass the government's budget plan could cause prices to firm on speculation.
"Passing the budget is good news, but I don't know if it will affect the market, with holidays coming up soon," said Victor Pitaleff of Moscow brokerage Renaissance Capital.
"Brokers will probably mark up prices in the first half of the day tomorrow, but prices will not rise much."
Utility Mosenergo, one of the most liquid shares in the market, saw less than $100,000 turnover on Sunday to close at $0.972 after $0.971 on December 11, before an end-of week holiday.
A trader at a Western brokerage said markets, sluggish in any case at end of year, did not see Sunday's vote as proof the budget would pass.
"It is still a close call. This is just the first reading," he said.

The budget, with a deficit of 3.5 percent of GDP, must pass second and third readings, scheduled for December 25, and Communist Party leader Gennady Zyuganov has said he reserved the right to block the bill if 11 conditions were not met.

Communists want back wage payments, increased government support of domestic industry -- both of which Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin has promised, to some degree -- and the ouster of Kremlin chief of staff Anatoly Chubais.
Communists have made similar calls for Chubais' dismissal for months.

Russian markets are also winding down for a long holiday covering Western and Russian Christmas and New Year, and market participants have said traders are unlikely to risk substantial profits by speculation in the last few weeks of the year.

Government T-bills firmed on the budget news, with average yields dropping to 37.5-39.9 percent from 39 and 41 percent early last week, and could firm further, traders said, but added the trend was unlikely to continue through the end of the year.

"Everyone expected the budget would be passed, although it does not change much. All the same, at the end of the year you have to raise money to pay taxes," said National Reserve Bank's Konstantin Demchenko, saying banks were likely to sell paper.

The rouble traded sporadically in a range of 5,538-5,540 for tomorrow settlement over the weekend, which were working days in Russia after a holiday on Thursday and Friday, but the market closed before the budget was approved.

Prices of MinFin bonds edged down slightly over the weekend, Tranche 4 easing to 59.85-60.15 from 60.00-60.25 on Wednesday, and trade was too thin to give a good indication of future trends, though dealers said they could firm on budget news.
